transcript:
Meeting header:
2028-05-10 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 min | Notes: POC scoping for private networking & data residency
Attendees: Evan Park (Redwood AE), Samir Kulkarni (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (CTO, BlueBay), Mark Lewis (Network Ops), Sasha Nguyen (PM)

Summary: quick sync to agree networking approach (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), residency regions, constraints around egress and HIPAA-like controls, and to agree a POC scope and timeline.

00:00 Evan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate it. Quick intros?
00:06 Priya (BlueBay): Hi I'm Priya, CTO at BlueBay — overseeing infra and data.
00:09 Mark (BlueBay): Mark, network ops, I'll own the connectivity bits.
00:12 Sasha (BlueBay): Sasha, PM for the conversational assistant project.
00:15 Evan: Great. Samir's our SE, he'll run the benchmark plan. Samir?
00:20 Samir (Redwood): Hi all, hi Priya, Mark — I'll focus on perf, kernel choices, and also the private deployment checklist.

01:05 Evan: To frame this, BlueBay wants to run Redwood in a private networking mode — basically no public endpoints, traffic over private connectivity, and guarantees on data residency. We want to scope the POC: success criteria, regions, benchmarks, and timeline.

01:40 Priya: Correct. We need to keep PHI inside approved regions (US-East and EU-West ideally). Also egress must be tightly controlled — we have proxy and firewall rules and we want to avoid burst egress charges or accidental public egress.

02:10 Mark: Operationally we prefer AWS PrivateLink over VPC peering in our org because of cross-account routing policies, but we also use peering for some partners. We'll decide after we see the runbook.

02:35 Samir: Quick callout: PrivateLink gives you per-service endpoints and avoids route table complexity; peering can be simpler and cheaper but may require additional routing controls. Both are supported by Redwood Private. We typically publish two options in the runbook.

03:10 Sasha: Are there differences in latency or throughput between PrivateLink and peering? That matters for our interactive chat SLA.

03:20 Samir: Good question. PrivateLink adds a small extra hop — in our tests typical added latency is 5-15ms compared to peering within the same region; throughput is similar but you'll want to size ENIs and endpoints. For heavy throughput we recommend peering or colocated dedicated capacity.

04:00 Priya: Our SLA target for the assistant is 95th perc latency end-to-end <200ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and sustained throughput of 50 concurrent chat sessions. Is that achievable?

04:25 Samir: For 128-token prompts, the biggest contributors are model decode latency and network round trips. With our optimized runtime on g4dn/g5-like infra, we typically see model side latency of ~40-80ms for smaller models, end-to-end 95p around 120-180ms over peering in same AZ. Over PrivateLink add ~10ms. We'll put exact numbers in the benchmark plan. For 50 concurrent chat sessions we need to size batchers and GPUs; I'll propose a sizing that targets reserve for 60 to allow headroom.

05:30 Mark: Good. About egress — we have strict egress ACLs; we want to confirm Redwood's control plane won't route customer data out to third-party regions during runtime.

05:45 Evan: Redwood Private can be deployed with a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC (we also offer a private control plane option). For the hosted control plane we do not recommend for PHI. For Private, all inference traffic can stay in your VPC; control plane communications are limited and we support bringing your own KMS. We'll share the security docs and a network diagram that highlights control-plane endpoints and required egress rules.

06:30 Priya: Can you confirm we can use our KMS/HSM for key management, and that logs can be retained in our account?

06:45 Samir: Yes — BYOK via AWS KMS is supported. Audit logs and metrics can be forwarded to your CloudWatch/S3. We'll include the exact S3 bucket policy examples.

07:15 Sasha: For the POC dataset — we plan to provide de-identified clinical notes and a small set of live anonymized queries. We also want to test hallucination rates and accuracy on our prompt sets.

07:40 Samir: Perfect. For benchmarks we'll run 3 phases: 1) baseline single-instance latency, 2) concurrent session scaling test (50-100 concurrent), and 3) cost/throughput curve with batching and quantization configs. We'll include quality checks against your prompt sets.

08:30 Evan: Timeline idea: 6-week POC. Week 1 — network onboarding + infra provisioning. Week 2 — baseline perf tests. Week 3 — scale tests and run quality evals. Week 4-5 — iterate on batch/quantization and routing. Week 6 — final report and decision. Thoughts?

09:05 Priya: That sounds reasonable. Can we compress to 4 weeks if provisioning is fast? Our Q3 roadmap would prefer faster turnaround.

09:20 Mark: Provisioning depends on approvals. If we do PrivateLink it's often faster for cross-account setups. Peering requires some networking approvals and route table changes.

09:40 Samir: We'll prepare both backlog runs. For a 4-week compressed POC we'd combine some steps: baseline and scale in week 1-2 and extend tuning into weeks 3-4. We can also run some synthetic benchmarks before full infra is up to validate perf expectations.

10:10 Sasha: On success criteria: we'll set three buckets — Performance (95p latency <200ms for short prompts; 99p <350ms), Throughput (support 50 concurrent sessions with <5% error rate), and Security (no public egress, KMS BYOK, SOC2 artifacts).

10:45 Samir: Agree. For cost evaluation we'll provide a per-token cost estimate for the config that meets your perf targets, and a lower-cost config for offline/low-priority workloads.

11:10 Priya: Any constraints on regions? We need EU-West data residency for EU customers and US-East for US. Can Redwood run multiple region endpoints in Private?

11:25 Evan: Yes, Private supports multi-region deployments; you can pin models/instances per region. For the POC we suggest starting in one region (US-East) and replicate to EU-West if routing and egress look good. We'll also document cross-region replication considerations.

12:00 Mark: Network details we'll share: VPC CIDRs (10.10.0.0/16 for infra), peering preferences, and an inventory of NAT/Proxy egress rules. We need to know which ports and internal FQNs Redwood needs for telemetry/control plane.

12:25 Samir: We'll send a minimal ports list, plus the runbook shows how to lock down control plane to specific IPs and how to use PrivateLink endpoints for control if you want zero public egress.

13:05 Evan: A couple of gotchas from other customers — if you use PrivateLink and TLS termination happens on Redwood side you should validate cert chain and SNI behavior; and if you have strict MTU or jumbo frames, some networking paths can show fragmentation. We'll include notes.

14:00 Priya: Good to know. On compliance, can you share SOC2 and any ISO docs? Also, will you sign a BAA?

14:15 Evan: We'll share SOC2 Type II reports and an enterprise security pack. BAAs are negotiable at the enterprise contract stage; for the POC we can do a limited scoping agreement; I'll ask legal to confirm.

15:00 Sasha: For benchmarks, what tooling will you use? JMeter? Custom scripts?

15:10 Samir: We'll use a mix: lightweight load harness we provide (python-based), locust for session-style scaling, and our internal token-level tracer for latency breakdowns. We'll give scripts you can run from a bastion in your VPC to avoid public egress.

16:00 Mark: Perf instrumentation — we want to see token-level breakdowns and per-route cost. Is that available in the POC?

16:10 Samir: Yes, our telemetry will emit per-request token counts, model variant used, end-to-end latency, and per-token cost estimates. We'll redact any content in telemetry if you prefer content-not-logged.

17:00 Priya: Ok next steps recap?

17:05 Evan: We'll send runbook, security pack, and benchmark plan. Samir will attach sample scripts and perf expectations. BlueBay will send CIDRs, preferred PrivateLink vs peering choice, and the prompt sets. We'll schedule a network deep-dive for next week.

17:35 Priya: Thanks. If we can get the runbook and scripts quickly we'll aim to kick off provisioning the week of 2028-05-15.

17:45 Evan: Perfect. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. Thanks everyone.

17:50 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: Automated transcript has occasional filler and mis-attributions; edited minimally for readability but kept timestamps every ~1-2 minutes.
